name: ByteKeel PixTag
author: ByteKeel

sections.description:
Fix the missing alt text and titles of your WordPress images from meaningful file names, one image at a time or in bulk, and keep the text that people already wrote. No AI or API key required.

ByteKeel PixTag reads what is already on your site: the file name of each image, its title and, if you use a template, the post it belongs to. It turns that into alt text (and, if you keep the option on, an image title) and writes it to the standard WordPress fields. Everything runs on your own server.

It does not look at the picture. When a file name says nothing about the image, ByteKeel PixTag writes nothing and marks the image “Needs review”, so a person can describe it.

Features

  • Clean text from file names. “red-leather-sofa-scaled.jpg” becomes “Red Leather Sofa”. The “-scaled”, “-rotated”, “-1024×768” and “-e1699999999999” parts that WordPress adds, numbers, extensions and repeated separators are removed. Non-Latin file names (for example Cyrillic or Japanese) keep their characters.
  • Camera and device names are not turned into alt text. Names such as IMG_1234, DSC01234, PXL_20241112_153012345, DJI_0042, “Screenshot 2026-11-12 at 10.30.45”, hashes, UUIDs and plain numbers produce no text. The image is marked “Needs review” instead.
  • Titles and templates. If the file name is not useful but the image has a real title, the title is used. Context templates build text from %filename%, %posttitle%, %sitetitle%, %category%, %tag%, %author%, %date% and %postexcerpt%. The hybrid method tries the template first, then the file name.
  • Keeps what people wrote. The Media Library action and the “only images missing alt text” bulk scope never change existing alt text. A title you wrote is not replaced either.
  • Bulk processor. Process every image that is missing alt text, with live progress, a log of what changed and a Stop button. Images already processed keep their alt text if you stop. Choose “all images” only if you want to replace existing alt text.
  • Media Library. An “Alt Text” status column (with “Needs review”), a “Generate Alt Text” bulk action and a Generate button on each image.
  • Dashboard and activity log. Counts of images with and without alt text and a log of each generation, stored in your own database.
  • Developer hooks. Filters for the generated text, template variables and generation methods.

More from ByteKeel

ByteKeel PixTag is made by ByteKeel. It is free and complete as it is. ByteKeel also publishes separate, paid plugins: ByteKeel PixTag Pro (AI image descriptions and alt text added on upload), TurboCache (page cache and optimization for Divi and WordPress) and Divi Smart Popup (popups for Divi). None of them is needed to use ByteKeel PixTag.

What it does not do

  • It does not describe what is in a picture.
  • It does not add alt text automatically when you upload an image or save a post. Run it from the Media Library or the bulk processor.
  • It does not change the alt text that blocks, page builders or themes keep inside post content.

Usage

One image. In Media > Library (list view) use the Generate button next to an image, or the Generate Alt Text button on its edit screen. This replaces the alt text of that one image, because you asked for it.

Several images. In Media > Library (list view) select images, choose “Generate Alt Text” in Bulk actions and click Apply. Images that already have alt text are skipped.

The whole library. Open ByteKeel PixTag > Bulk Processor, choose “Only images missing alt text” and click Start Processing. Use “All images, replacing existing alt text” only when you want to start over.

Images marked “Needs review”. These images have file names that do not describe them. Open them from the Dashboard or the Bulk Processor (“Show them in the Media Library”), and write the alt text yourself. After you change the settings (for example a template that uses the post title) you can run only these images again from the Bulk Processor.

Privacy

ByteKeel PixTag does not send any data out of your site and does not use any external service. It makes no requests to other servers, sets no cookies and adds nothing to your public pages.

It stores data only in your own WordPress database: its settings, an activity log (date, image ID, method, result) that you can switch off in Settings, short-lived progress data while a bulk run is open, and a small marker on images that need review.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New, search for “ByteKeel PixTag”, click Install Now and then Activate. Or upload the plugin folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Open ByteKeel PixTag > Settings and choose a generation method: file name, context template or hybrid.
  3. Try the Generate button on one image in Media > Library (list view) and check the result.
  4. Run ByteKeel PixTag > Bulk Processor for the rest of your library.
sections.faq:
Do I need an AI service or an API key?

No. ByteKeel PixTag generates text on your own server from file names, titles and post information. No image or text is sent anywhere.

Will it overwrite alt text I wrote myself?

Not unless you ask it to. The bulk scope “only images missing alt text” and the Media Library bulk action skip images that already have alt text. Two actions replace existing alt text because you chose them: the bulk scope “All images”, and the Generate button on a single image. A title you wrote is kept in every case.

What happens with file names like IMG_1234.jpg or Screenshot 2026-11-12.png?

Nothing is written from the file name. If the image has a meaningful title, that title is used. Otherwise the alt text stays empty and the image is marked “Needs review” in the Media Library and on the Dashboard.

Does it work with WooCommerce product images?

ByteKeel PixTag works on the file names of any image in the Media Library. Product images with names such as blue-cotton-t-shirt-1.jpg or black-leather-wallet-1024×1024.jpg become “Blue Cotton T-Shirt” and “Black Leather Wallet”. It does not read product attributes.

Does it add alt text when I upload an image?

No. Run the Media Library bulk action, the Generate button or the Bulk Processor.

Which fields does it write?

Alt text, and the image title when that option is on (it is by default). A title that is already meaningful is left alone.

Can I undo a bulk run?

There is no automatic undo. The activity log lists every change. Try a few images first with the Generate button.

Does it work with page builders?

ByteKeel PixTag writes the standard WordPress alt text field of the image. Anything that reads that field, such as the block editor and most builders and themes, shows it.

Does it slow down my site?

It loads nothing on your public pages. Generation runs in the admin area.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

By default nothing: settings and the activity log stay. Turn on “Delete data on uninstall” in Settings to remove them. Alt text written to your images is never removed.

Is there a Pro version?

ByteKeel also publishes ByteKeel PixTag Pro, a separate plugin that adds AI image descriptions with your own API key and automatic alt text on upload. ByteKeel PixTag does not need it. See https://bytekeel.com/products/bytekeel-pixtag-pro
sections.changelog:
1.0.11

  • First release on WordPress.org.
  • File names: removes -scaled, -rotated, -1024×768, -e1699999999999, @2x, copy and (2) suffixes, version marks and repeated separators; keeps non-Latin characters; “t shirt” becomes “T-Shirt”.
  • Camera, phone and screenshot names (IMG_1234, DSC01234, PXL_…, DJI_…, Screenshot …), hashes, UUIDs and plain numbers no longer become alt text: the image is marked “Needs review”.
  • A meaningful attachment title is used when the file name is not.
  • Hand-written alt text and titles are kept; running a bulk action again gives the same result.
  • New “Needs review” column text, Dashboard count, Media Library filter and Bulk Processor scope.
